 Aparna Yadav urges keeping Lord Ram and Krishna out of elections 
 By
 TNM (With ANI Inputs) 
 ✓
 19 November 2026, 5:20 pm 
 3 min read
 19 Nov 2026 
 ANI Photo | Aparna Yadav urges keeping Lord Ram and Krishna out of elections 
 Uttar Pradesh State Commission for Women Vice-Chairperson Aparna Yadav has emphasised that Lord Ram and Lord Krishna are matters of faith and should not be involved in electoral politics. Speaking in Kanpur on November 19, she urged the public not to turn religious deities into subjects of election campaigns.
 Yadav highlighted the importance of constructing Lord Shri Ram’s temple for the Sanatan tradition, while noting that the Lord Shri Krishna temple has already been built and the government had decided some time ago to enhance it. “It’s not an issue, it’s a matter of our faith. And the construction of Lord Shri Ram’s temple was essential for Sanatan. Similarly, the temple of Lord Shri Krishna has already been built, and the government decided a long time ago to improve it. This is not an election issue. So, I also request everyone, please don’t make this an election issue. Lord Ram and Krishna are our deities and will always remain so,” she said.

 Addressing questions about Bharatiya Janata Party election slogans and posters, Yadav stated that slogans serve to raise public enthusiasm during elections.
 Regarding Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya’s invitation to Akhilesh Yadav to visit Mathura, she described it as a positive initiative and encouraged acceptance of such invitations. “Respected Keshav ji is a senior member of our Bharatiya Janata Party and currently the Deputy CM, and I will just say that he has made a good initiative. To always promote the Sanatan culture and expand the religion, such invitations are given, and everyone who has been invited should gladly accept his invitation,” she said.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 On the death of a minor student during a PDA roadshow the previous day, Yadav called the incident unfortunate and assured that strict action would be taken regardless of political affiliation. “It’s very unfortunate, and I will just say that strict action should be taken against whoever is responsible for it. Because whenever political rallies or such events take place, regardless of the party, on behalf of the Women’s Commission, I will ensure that the culprits involved in this are punished,” she asserted.
 During her visit to the grievance redressal centre, Yadav responded to concerns about restricted access and public availability of statistics by stating that entry is regulated by law and constitutional provisions. She reported that construction work was ongoing at the centre.
 Yadav also shared that two young girls, approximately one and a half years old and 11 months respectively, who were abandoned by their parents, are now being placed in suitable adoptive homes.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Regarding the Women’s Commission’s statistics, she said all data would be made public following official instructions. She recalled that after taking oath on September 4, 2024, the 28-member commission, including its president, vice-president, and members, had resolved 20,000 pending cases in approximately 20 days.
